correctness.rationale: For every star S_t with t>=3 the three-round centre/leaf mapping is a partial isomorphism; the disjoint-union component response can visit at most three components of any kind, proving a size-nonincreasing reduction to all 255 nonzero profiles with four coordinates 0..3. For each finite graph G, iterated extension sets of all six equality/adjacency atoms on triples are exactly the rank-three Hintikka type by induction on remaining moves. The attached reproducible program directly enumerates 255 such graphs, obtains 22 distinct exact type values, and minimizes the vertex order within every class. The maximum minimum is 9, for three P3 components; the reduction transfers this lower bound to all star forests. A logically separate recursive three-round EF minimax verifies non-equivalence of all 231 pairs of class representatives and four selected comparisons. Experiments alone are not an infinite proof; the disjoint-union strategy supplies the unbounded part.

originality.rationale: No source examined states the complete 22-theory classification or its sharp 9-vertex rank-three kernel. Published general EF-game theorems prove the criterion, not the exact star-forest quotient; the 1989 star-arboricity literature concerns a different invariant. Results on finite equivalence relations and 2-regular graphs address different relational structures and do not give this star-forest graph-language classification as a quantifier-rank-preserving corollary. Numerical similarity with an equivalence-relation kernel is explicitly considered and is not treated as originality evidence. There is a real residual risk of an unindexed specialized calculation or folklore.
residual_risks: An unindexed or informal exact rank-three classification of star forests could predate this computation.

value.rationale: The infinite class of star forests is natural in sparse-graph decomposition (star arboricity), and precise indistinguishability under three quantifiers is a motivated finite-model theory invariant for model checking. The classification determines the full natural quotient, not a narrow ad-hoc parameter slice: 22 concrete possible theories, a uniform nine-vertex normal form, and a sharp extremizer comprising three two-leaf stars. The 255-case census is coupled to an all-size theorem, and a matching lower bound is supplied; the result is not justified by code reproducibility or novelty alone.
